_comment: Capture conditions per gesture session. Written by auto_collect_dataset.py
for new sessions; A, B and C are backfilled from what the repository
records -- capture timestamps in the image filenames, the photometry
derived by audit_claims.d_capture_conditions, and the condition
descriptions in the manuscript. Fields that were never recorded are null
rather than estimated: nominal_distance_m in particular was not controlled
across A, B and C, which is itself a finding (Section V-C attributes the

nominal_distance_m is null for A-C because no single distance applies: the operator deliberately varied standoff across 0.5-2.0 m within each session so the dataset would span scales. That is a design choice, not an uncontrolled variable, and it decorrelates apparent hand size from class label - which is the real reason the two scale-derived classes transfer worst.

A.distance_protocol: deliberately varied across 0.5-2.0 m during capture, to train across scales; not held fixed and not logged per frame

B.background_description: domestic room, background close to skin tone
B.distance_protocol: deliberately varied across 0.5-2.0 m during capture, to train across scales; not held fixed and not logged per frame

C.distance_protocol: deliberately varied across 0.5-2.0 m during capture, to train across scales; not held fixed and not logged per frame
